title: How Sponsors Calculated Prevalence for FDA Orphan Drug Designation and Where FDA Pushed Back
summary: The prevalence methods sponsors of approved rare-disease drugs used for FDA orphan designation, and the population definitions that drew OOPD questions or revocations.
body_markdown:
## How sponsors calculated prevalence for FDA orphan drug designation, and where FDA pushed back


FDA's orphan drug designation depends on one number: fewer than 200,000 affected persons in the United States[41](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=41) . The designation files for approved drugs that appear in Drugs@FDA review packages show that sponsors reached that number in a small set of repeatable ways. The same records show that FDA's Office of Orphan Products Development (OOPD) usually objected to how the sponsor defined the population, not to the arithmetic. The costliest disputes came from subsets that were too narrow, patient groups left out of the count, outdated denominators and claims data likely to undercount cases, and, for rare pediatric disease requests, the wrong age metric. In two pediatric-hypertension cases, designations granted in January 2013 and October 2015 were revoked on April 28, 2016, a few months before FDA approved Qbrelis (July 2016) and Epaned oral solution (September 2016).


### The standard FDA applies


- **Point prevalence of diagnosed patients.** Prevalence is the total number of patients with the disease at a given time (point prevalence). Incidence, by contrast, counts newly diagnosed patients over a period such as a year[64](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=64) . For a therapeutic drug, FDA counts individuals in the United States who have been diagnosed with the disease or condition[41](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=41) .
- **Genetic conditions.** When a genetic abnormality is present from birth but clinical disease appears later, or never, who counts as "diagnosed" depends on the intended use. The product may treat the abnormality itself, prevent or slow progression, or treat the manifestations[41](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=41) .
- **Vaccines, diagnostics and preventive drugs.** These use a different denominator: the number of persons of all ages in the United States who will receive the drug each year[41](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=41) .
- **Timing.** The estimate must be below 200,000 when the request is submitted[63](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=63) . FDA generally does not re-evaluate prevalence at NDA/BLA submission. It may revisit the determination if relevant information that existed at the time of the request was not provided or was not known to FDA[62](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=62) .
- **Documentation.** Requests should include authoritative references, a list of sources, and the dates of the information provided[63](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=63) . 21 CFR 316.20(b)(8) requires information on the prevalence of the target population[205](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=205) .
- **Orphan subsets.** For a disease affecting 200,000 or more persons, a drug qualifies only for a subset in which use outside the subset would be inappropriate because of a property of the drug, such as toxicity, mechanism of action or prior clinical experience[48](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=48)[33](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=33) . Defining a narrower patient group is not enough on its own. The sponsor must show why the remaining patients are not appropriate candidates[48](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=48) .
- **Grounds for deficiency or denial.** FDA may issue a deficiency letter if information is missing, inaccurate or incomplete[62](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=62) . It may deny a request if prevalence is 200,000 or more and there is no valid subset, if the evidence does not support the estimate or the subset, or if material facts are untrue or omitted[65](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=65) .


FDA's guidance on rare disease drug development makes a related point, though it expressly does not apply to designation requests. It says prevalence estimates vary with case definition, geography, and advances in diagnosis and treatment. It recommends citing individual current estimates rather than calculated averages[56](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=56) .


### Methods sponsors used in approved rare-disease programs


Method Example (drug, condition) How the number was built FDA response


Birth incidence × annual births × life expectancy Vimizim (elosulfase alfa), Morquio A / MPS IVA 1/200,000 × 4,000,000 U.S. births/year × 40-year assumed life expectancy = no more than 800 patients[75](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=75) OOPD accepted prevalence below 200,000. It had previously accepted a higher estimate of 1,532 in designation #09-2808[75](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=75)


Same model, used by the FDA reviewer as a cross-check Mepsevii (vestronidase alfa), MPS VII Sponsor estimated 1,300. The reviewer applied 1/250,000 incidence (NIH Genetics Home Reference) × 4 million births = 16 cases/year, × 50-year life expectancy = 800[137](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=137) Accepted[137](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=137)


Disease registry / foundation data report Symdeko (tezacaftor/ivacaftor), cystic fibrosis Approximately 29,000, taken from the Cystic Fibrosis Foundation 2015 annual data report[87](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=87) Consistent with OOPD's own figure of approximately 30,000[87](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=87)


Published prevalence rate × U.S. population Rivfloza (nedosiran), primary hyperoxaluria type 1 Applicant's estimate of 2,692 U.S. patients, based on a 2018 U.S. population of 327 million. The review also cites a global prevalence of 1 to 3 per million, which would give only about 330 to 980[195](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=195) No prevalence issue recorded[195](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=195)


Published rates converted to counts, by phenotype Kanuma (sebelipase alfa), LAL deficiency Wolman disease: 1 per 528,000 births (about 600 U.S. patients). CESD: 1/40,000 to 1/300,000 (about 1,055 to 7,925)[135](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=135) Orphan designation granted July 1, 2010[135](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=135)


Prior OOPD-accepted estimate carried forward Cholbam (cholic acid), bile acid synthesis disorders 500 patients. OOPD expected little growth since its 2003 review[132](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=132) Accepted[132](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=132)


Annual procedure volume (diagnostic use) ChiRhoStim (synthetic human secretin) Added OOPD-determined annual ERCP and MRCP counts to pancreatic ultrasonography volume. A second, "more conservative" build combined disease prevalence, cancer incidence and procedure volumes[69](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=69) Granted because even the maximum annual estimate was below the threshold[69](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=69)


Incidence used as prevalence for an acute condition Defitelio (defibrotide), hepatic VOD About 20,000 HSCTs/year × 13.7% VOD incidence = 2,740 cases/year. No more than 9,240/year under high-end assumptions[214](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=214)[74](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=74) Treated as consistent with the prior designation request[74](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=74)


Annual incidence of a one-time treatment setting Ellence (epirubicin), adjuvant breast cancer 1997 incidence of Stage II node-positive (40,753) plus Stage III (15,975) = 56,728[1](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=1) . The sponsor argued annual incidence equaled prevalence because the drug is given once, with a cumulative-dose ceiling set by cardiotoxicity[196](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=196) Initially denied, later designated (see below)[7](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=7)[197](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=197)


Some records disclose only the result of the estimate. Hetlioz's sponsor cited 65,000 to 95,000 U.S. patients with non-24-hour sleep-wake disorder, without a documented derivation[144](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=144) . Sucraid's projection of 100 to 500 patients rested on one physician's referral experience, and it appeared in a post-approval letter rather than a documented designation calculation[103](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=103) .


### Methods that drew FDA questions, refusals or revocations


#### 1. Subsets defined by market or preference rather than by the drug


- **Epaned (enalapril oral solution), pediatric hypertension.** The sponsor proposed counting only children prescribed enalapril, particularly those aged 10 to 14 and younger who would need a liquid[20](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=20) . OOPD rejected this. The condition was pediatric hypertension as a whole, and a subset needs an intrinsic drug property that precludes use outside it. User preference for a liquid over tablets does not qualify[20](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=20) .
- **Defitelio, hepatic VOD.** The sponsor limited its population to post-HSCT VOD. OOPD said a narrower intended marketing indication cannot, on its own, restrict the population. Unless a product feature prevented broader use, the count had to include all hepatic VOD[74](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=74) . The sponsor's rationale was that post-HSCT VOD had the most favorable benefit-risk and that no data existed in other settings. It agreed to recalculate across the entire hepatic VOD population[74](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=74) .
- **Ellence (epirubicin), Stage II node-positive and Stage III breast cancer.** In an April 16, 1999 letter, FDA found the stage-defined group was not a medically plausible subset. FDA saw no evidence that epirubicin worked only in those stages or that those patients were uniquely responsive. It counted all patients who could benefit from adjuvant or palliative chemotherapy (Stages I to IV), about 1,993,000[7](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=7) . OOPD denied the request on July 26, 1999[202](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=202)[14](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=14) . The sponsor argued that adjuvant and metastatic disease are distinct clinical settings and cited prior orphan designations in metastatic breast cancer[196](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=196) . FDA's oncology and drug evaluation offices then agreed. In August 1999 minutes they described adjuvant therapy as distinct and the population as medically plausible, because the drug is used once, for less than a year, with use limited by cardiac toxicity[199](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=199) . FDA designated epirubicin on September 14, 1999[197](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=197) and confirmed seven-year exclusivity for the adjuvant, node-positive indication[201](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=201) . The subset argument succeeded once it rested on properties of the drug (cumulative cardiotoxicity, single use) rather than on labeling scope.


#### 2. Leaving out patients the sponsor itself planned to treat


- **Genotropin (somatropin), growth failure in children born small for gestational age.** The sponsor's estimate excluded children treated during puberty, even though it described continued therapy through puberty as part of the expected treatment outcome[78](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=78) . On June 29, 2000, OOPD found that including pubertal children would push the population over the threshold. It held further review in abeyance, required a response within 90 days, and asked for supporting references with any resubmission[78](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=78) .


#### 3. Outdated denominators and claims data likely to undercount (resulting in revocation)


The pediatric hypertension designations for Qbrelis (lisinopril oral solution) and Epaned are the clearest cautionary cases.


- An earlier lisinopril oral solution request (designation #12-3655; the holder's name is redacted in the review), submitted in February 2012 and covering primary hypertension with complications plus secondary hypertension, reported a prevalence of 196,453 and was granted in January 2015[76](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=76) . Silvergate's own requests, dated July 2012 (enalapril) and May 2015 (lisinopril), led to designation #12-3767, granted January 30, 2013[17](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=17) , and designation #15-4819 (ages 0 to 16), granted October 14, 2015[3](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=3) .
- FDA consulted its Division of Pediatric and Maternal Health (DPMH) on the lisinopril estimate. DPMH identified four problems:


- The sponsor used the 2010 Census pediatric population instead of 2014 data[68](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=68) .
- No U.S. publication directly estimated how many children with primary hypertension need drug therapy after lifestyle measures fail[67](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=67) .
- The sponsor relied on a cross-sectional, ICD-9 claims-based study that likely underdiagnosed hypertension and used a definition less rigorous than NHBPEP criteria[70](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=70) .
- That study was limited to privately insured children at a single national insurer, so it may not represent U.S. children demographically or socioeconomically[70](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=70) .


- DPMH's independent estimate was 1,265,495 children with primary hypertension and 590,304 to 927,309 with secondary hypertension[70](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=70) . DPMH showed that even if only 15.8% of its 1,265,495 primary-hypertension estimate (which the review describes as obese U.S. children) needed drugs, the total would be 199,949, essentially at the threshold. Its clinical view was that the true share is far higher[68](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=68) .
- In a separate reconstruction, OOPD started from 70.8 million U.S. children aged 0 to 16, applied the 3.6% hypertension prevalence from Hansen et al., and then the 15.8% of those children who had a true hypertension diagnosis in the medical record, giving 402,710 diagnosed children[83](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=83) . Secondary hypertension alone came to 203,107 to 257,452 (or 208,201 using another Flynn estimate), which exceeds 200,000 before primary hypertension is counted[6](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=6) .
- OOPD proposed revocation of both designations on April 8, 2016. Silvergate chose not to respond, and FDA revoked both designations on April 28, 2016 under 21 CFR 316.29(a)(3). Benefits were terminated because the designations had been improperly granted[3](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=3)[17](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=17) . OOPD stressed that prevalence is measured as of the date of the request, using documentation available by then[73](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=73) .
- DPMH also recommended reviewing other pediatric hypertension designations granted after February 2014 and declining future requests unless there is conclusive evidence of prevalence below 200,000[70](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=70) .


#### 4. Unsupported assertions


- **ChiRhoStim.** The sponsor claimed that historical U.S. secretin use was below a certain annual number but supplied no source data[69](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=69) . The request was granted anyway, because even its maximum procedure-based estimate was under the threshold[69](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=69) . An unsupported figure did not sink this request, but it added nothing to it.


#### 5. A disease plainly above the threshold


- **Entocort EC (budesonide), Crohn's disease.** OOPD denied the request because U.S. Crohn's disease prevalence was about 370,300[11](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=11) . The record does not show a subset argument that could have saved it[11](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=11) .


### Rare pediatric disease requests: a separate pediatric test


Rare pediatric disease designation (the basis for the priority review voucher) adds a second requirement: the disease must be serious or life-threatening, and its serious or life-threatening manifestations must primarily affect individuals aged 0 through 18. Under FDA's 2019 draft guidance, onset in childhood is not enough. FDA assesses which manifestations primarily affect children, weighing the timing and rate of progression, effects on growth and development, and whether the proportion of children with a manifestation exceeds the proportion of adults[220](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=220) . The Cholbam, Defitelio and Vimizim reviews below (2014 to 2016) predate that guidance and weighed the age share of the affected population; the Defitelio reviewer, for example, required that more than 50% of cases be in people under 19[221](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=221) . Read their percentages as decisions under that older reading, not as the current test. Several approved-drug records show sponsors getting this wrong.


- **Cholbam.** The sponsor relied on age at diagnosis. OOPD required the current age distribution of all diagnosed U.S. residents living with the disease. OOPD then obtained data showing that 69% were under 18[185](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=185) .
- **Defitelio.** The sponsor relied on pediatric CIBMTR VOD rates of 9.2% (2008 to 2014) and 6.1% (2014), compared with 2.2% and 1.56% in adults, and on a 61.1% pediatric share in expanded-access Study 2006-05[212](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=212) . The chemotherapy-associated VOD figure of 79.7% pediatric used a cutoff of 16 years or younger, not the required 18[213](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=213) . The reviewer also found problems with the underlying data. Extrapolating CIBMTR's research-level subset to all U.S. centers was inaccurate, because the share of patients selected for research varied by year[215](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=215) . The published incidence studies were mostly non-U.S. and used varying diagnostic criteria[215](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=215) . FDA concluded that hepatic VOD had not been shown to primarily affect people from birth through 18 and denied the voucher[209](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=209)[211](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=211)[219](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=219) .
- **Vimizim.** By contrast, registry, natural-history and Phase 3 data showing 64% to 80% of patients aged 18 or younger were accepted. So was reasoning from onset at ages 1 to 3 and shortened survival[75](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=75) .
- **Exondys 51 (eteplirsen).** FDA told the sponsor at a pre-NDA meeting that prevalence estimates are a critical element of any rare pediatric disease voucher request[86](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=86) .
- **Post-approval reporting.** Recent voucher approvals require sponsors to report, for each of the first four years after approval, estimates of the total U.S. disease population and the population aged 0 to 18, along with demand and actual distribution. Examples include Evrysdi[158](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=158) , Daybue[170](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=170) and Xolremdi[160](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=160) .


### Practical lessons from the record


1. **Define the disease before the market.** OOPD consistently counted the whole disease or condition unless a drug property limited use. A labeling strategy, a formulation preference or trial eligibility was not enough (Epaned, Defitelio, Ellence)[20](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=20)[74](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=74)[7](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=7) . FDA's device-side guidance on HUD subsets lists trial eligibility, a planned narrow indication, unmet need, standard of care and price as insufficient on their own[47](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=47) . That guidance concerns devices, not orphan drugs.
2. **Count everyone the drug is expected to treat.** Leaving out planned treatment phases, such as puberty for Genotropin, brought a refusal[78](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=78) .
3. **Use current denominators, and question sources that undercount.** Outdated Census data and single-payer claims data were central to the pediatric hypertension revocations[68](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=68)[70](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=70)[3](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=3) .
4. **Match the metric to the condition.** Point prevalence of diagnosed patients is the default[64](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=64)[41](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=41) . Annual counts apply to diagnostics, vaccines and preventive drugs[41](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=41) . Acute conditions were handled with annual incidence in the Defitelio review[74](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=74) .
5. **Show your work with dated, cited sources.** FDA expects authoritative references with dates[63](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=63) . Unsupported figures (ChiRhoStim's historical-use claim) carried no weight[69](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=69) .
6. **Leave margin under 200,000.** Estimates close to the threshold, such as the 196,453 in the pediatric hypertension history, did not survive FDA's independent reanalysis[76](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=76)[6](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=6) . A designation granted on such an estimate can be revoked later if the evidence available at the time of the request shows the population was larger[62](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=62)[3](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=3) .


The Drugs@FDA review packages rarely reproduce the full designation request. For many orphan-designated products (for example, Darzalex, Uptravi and Spevigo), the record confirms designation but not how the sponsor estimated prevalence[155](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=155)[111](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=111)[112](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/sponsors-calculated-prevalence-for-fda-orphan-drug?showSourceNumber=112) . These cases therefore show patterns in how OOPD reasons. They are not a complete catalogue of accepted methods.
